Evidence before equations

Data with a clear provenance.

Measured numbers anchor the questions. Simple models make the calculus visible.

Published values

Measurements, dimensions, and specifications come from government agencies, official sites, manufacturers, and peer-reviewed papers. Each card below shows the values used and links to the original.

Teaching assumptions

Idealized shapes, profiles, and fields are listed under “We assume” in each problem. They are teaching models, not observations or engineering advice.

Exact mathematics

An answer can be exact for the model while the model is only an approximation of the real thing. State units, and say where the model falls short.

Source pages were consulted in November 2026. Published values are snapshots: the Monterey tide datums, for example, use the 1983–2001 epoch. No live data are used.

Shared conversions

1 ft = 0.3048 m · 1 US gal = 0.003785411784 m³ · 1 acre = 4046.8564224 m² · 1 day = 86,400 s

Problems use local Cartesian coordinates in the stated units, not raw latitude and longitude. The answer checker grades the stated model, not a real-world forecast.

Published climate index

NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ERSST.v6)

NOAA Climate Prediction Center, accessed November 17, 2026. The ONI is the 3-month running mean of SST anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region; El Niño periods use a threshold of +0.5 °C met for at least five overlapping seasons. CPC now notes that the Relative ONI (RONI) is used for official monitoring. The anomaly maps in the problem are models, not observed fields.

How the practice tools work

Answers, completed checks, hints, and discussion notes are stored only in this browser’s local storage. Math is rendered by a bundled local copy of MathJax. The site has no accounts, analytics, external math-rendering requests, or AI API. Solutions and expected answers are intentionally included in the site files; this is a learning aid rather than a secure assessment.

If browser storage is unavailable, all questions, hints, solutions, and answer checks still work for the current visit. Use “Reset this week” to clear one week’s saved work.

The checker supports elementary expressions and samples equivalent formula inputs at several test points; it does not constitute a proof of symbolic equivalence or evaluate written reasoning. The vector-potential construction is checked by numerically differentiating its components at several points and comparing the curl; it also checks the requested zero first component. Written reasoning and theorem hypotheses still need your own justification.
